subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should the direct `read` tool get a narrow binary-document fallback now, or should this wait for broader document parsing/provider-native file architecture?
rationale: Current source still has the reported token-waste behavior, but automatic parsing, provider-native forwarding, and a minimal fallback have different security and ownership boundaries.

options.title: Land Narrow Fallback
options.body: Review, repair, or replace the linked guard work so known PDF/Office document reads return a clear fallback message instead of decoded bytes.

options.title: Fold Into Document Architecture
options.body: Keep this open as context for the broader non-image document/provider-native attachment design and close the conflicting guard branch separately.

options.title: Docs-Only Tool Guidance
options.body: Update tool description and guidance to steer models away from binary document reads without changing runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Land Narrow Fallback
recommendation.body: Review, repair, or replace the linked guard work so known PDF/Office document reads return a clear fallback message instead of decoded bytes.

likelyOwner.reason: The current read-tool blame and repeated old pi-tools history make steipete the strongest available routing candidate for this product-boundary choice.
